goal: VC-201-073 (P0) claims mastery of: Propagate local-only, workspace-private, and approved-cloud labels through inference, MCP, A2A, generated tools, and artifacts; indirect delegation cannot strip a label to bypass an egress denial.. Its own narrative does not claim delivery: PARTIAL: secret detection and egress refusal are verified (`crates/susi-core/src/tests/prompt_secret_scan.rs`: positive_corpus_detects_vendor_prefixes, negative_corpus_keeps_benign_text, block_policy_refuses_egress, env_held_secret_is_detected) and A2A handler policy is checked (`crates/susi-gawd-a2a/src/lib.rs`: a2a_handler_module_policy). Residual: propagation of local-only / workspace-private /. Prove or refute it: add a nonzero test named vc_201_073_mastery_* that exercises the capability on its production path, and record exactly which part is missing when it cannot be proven. Coverage is not mastery: this closes only when the capability is verified, and a linked closed task is not evidence. Closing this task records the outcome, not a passing test: write .agents/roadmap-verdicts/<the vector>.json with verdict 'delivered' (and the test or record that proves it) or 'not-delivered' (with what is missing and the task ids that track the follow-up work), then run scripts/check-roadmap-verdict.py <the vector> — which is this task's acceptance. A refutation therefore closes the task and files the work, instead of stalling on a test that cannot pass; the roadmap and the queue both understand the record. Do not reserve .agents/roadmap-verdicts in your claim: the directory is exempt from the scope check precisely so a verdict commits under your source claim, and reserving it would overlap every other verification task and serialize them all. Reserve the source paths you will touch, and add a scope if the verdict needs to change the vector's narrative in .agents/roadmap.json.
